editorial.headline: Aerial Spraying and Pollination, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers specialised aircraft work for spraying and pollination under particular conditions, with full foreign ownership open nationally and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
Aerial spraying and pollination is a narrow, operationally specific activity. The record describes work carried out through the air, using special aircraft, when particular conditions require it. In plain English, this is not general agriculture, not general aviation, and not a broad land-service category. Its centre of gravity is the act itself: spraying or pollinating from the air by aircraft built or assigned for that kind of task.

That precision matters for founders because the activity is defined by method as much as by sector. The work is not simply “support for farming”; it is support delivered through aerial application. A business registering this activity is therefore presenting itself around specialised aircraft-based field service: the aircraft, the aerial route, and the condition-specific nature of the work are all part of the scope. The Indonesian title makes the same point compactly: jasa penyemprotan dan penyerbukan melalui udara.

The national investment picture is straightforward. The activity is marked TERBUKA, and the foreign ownership ceiling in the record is 100%. That means the national entry position is fully open to foreign ownership under the cited source, rather than open only to a capped minority stake. It is also open across the listed enterprise scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. The scale range is unusually broad in practical terms, but the record does not turn that into a licence rule, capital rule, or timing rule; it simply says the activity is available at those scales.

Bali is also usable on the record supplied. The province’s moratorium rule blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA registration island-wide, permanently, but this activity is not blocked by that rule. The Bali reason is explicit: at Besar scale the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it falls outside the moratorium block. That creates an honest reading: a foreign-owned company can treat this activity as nationally open and not Bali-blocked today, while recognising that the Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK rather than a low-risk pass.
